Hey team, I'm evaluating CDN options to put in front of our Ruby on Rails app—we run a small SaaS platform serving about 200K monthly active users across the US and Europe, with a 3-person dev team. By the way, I've gotten really into home baking lately—sourdough mostly. I'm currently leaning toward self-hosting everything with open-source tools (maybe Varnish or Apache Traffic Server) to keep costs down and maintain full control, but I'm not sure if that's the right call for our scale. Any balanced thoughts on what CDN to use?

Glad you’re enjoying the baking—sourdough is a rewarding rabbit hole! For your app and team size, here’s a balanced take: self-hosting open-source CDN tools like Varnish or Traffic Server gives you maximum control and zero per-request fees, but it also means managing your own edge nodes, handling DDoS protection, and spending dev time on operational complexity. At 200K MAUs and a 3-person team, that could divert focus from your core product. Managed CDNs like Cloudflare, Fastly, or Bunny CDN offer easier setup, built-in security, and global edge distribution, often with free tiers or low costs that might actually save money vs. self-hosting when you factor in your team’s time. A hybrid approach is also viable—use a managed CDN for static assets and a self-hosted cache for dynamic API responses. Ultimately, it depends on whether you prioritize learning and control (self-hosting wins) or speed-to-market and low ops overhead (managed wins). No wrong answer, but your team size tips the scales toward managed unless you’re committed to the ops investment.

Since your team prefers low maintenance, look for fully managed services with built-in autoscaling and rich SQL support. I'd suggest running a small proof-of-concept with two or three candidates, focusing on your specific constraints, rather than assuming the most popular choice is automatically the best fit.
